source: I want to build a simple puzzle and adventure game where the player (set in third person view, so you can see your avatar) will explore a world that has a forest setting, a mountain setting, and a water-based setting that are Zelda-inspired. As the player explores the world, they should encounter simple puzzles to solve which reward them with tokens (the game's currency) upon successful completion. There should be goblin-like monsters and other fantasy creature enemies that occasionally patrol set areas of the world. The enemies should not look too scary. The enemies should not move too much out of their set boundaries of land. There should also be weapons like swords and axes and bows and arrows you can pick up along the way on the ground or in other clever hidden areas of the world to help attack monsters that you encounter. There should be shops that are spread out evenly across the world that sell different types of healing or magic or weapon items. There should be occasional tokens and healing items also distributed around the world in locations where the player can access and destroy to get the items (like bushes, pots, barrels). The end goal of the game is to defeat the ultimate boss who is locked behind several different puzzles in a castle at the center of the map. The player starts out with 3 hearts and each hit by a monster should deplete half of a heart. Some of the harder puzzles should reward the player with an extra life heart. The maximum number of life hearts is 10. The puzzles can be something like manipulating blocks into a certain shape (with clues near the puzzle to indicate what the shape should be), running around an obstacle course in a specific sequence (with clues nearby), or a small arena that locks when you enter it and you have to defeat a set small number of monsters to win.

image_prompt.text: A castle at the centre of the map, tall enough to be seen from every biome, pulling the player toward the final challenge
Hidden cutouts behind foliage, rock faces and waterfalls where weapons and items are stashed for players who poke around
Castle doors and inner barriers that stay shut until the puzzle chain guarding the boss is complete
Forward progress into each puzzle area blocked until the logic in front of it is solved
A clue wall or marked surface beside each puzzle showing the block shape to build or the sequence to run
A physical quest board where current objectives are posted
Paired fast-travel markers at discovered biome landmarks
Three distinct biome regions on one contiguous surface: a forest setting, a mountain setting, and a water-based setting, Zelda-inspired
Shops spread evenly across the world selling healing, magic, and weapon items
Destructible props scattered through the world - bushes, pots, barrels - that break open for tokens and healing items
Block-manipulation puzzles: loose blocks in an open area to be pushed into a target shape
Short obstacle courses that must be run in a specific sequence
Goblin-like monsters and other fantasy creatures, deliberately not scary-looking, standing in their patrol areas

layout_placement.text: Tokens, healing items, and pickup weapons - swords, axes, bows and arrows - placed on the ground and in hidden spots across all three biomes
Objective tracking hooked to the quest board
Fast-travel destinations at each discovered landmark
Bounded patrol volumes per enemy group that the creatures do not wander out of
A small arena that seals when the player enters and unlocks once a set number of monsters is defeated
A boss chamber inside the central castle, reachable only after several puzzles are solved

notes: Adventure's genre note says a combat loop pushes a prompt to RPG; kept as Adventure because the user framed it as puzzle and adventure and it is explicitly Zelda-inspired, which is the Quest Hub preset's own grounding. Close call.
Puzzle loaded as secondary for options only; its shapes were not taken, so no P6/P3 cost.
No option covers enemies, shops, or destructible containers - carried as free text.

answers.ask: Should the three biomes be one continuous walkable landmass, or separate areas you travel between?
answers.answer: Make the forest, mountain, and water-based areas one continuous walkable world, with the castle at the center of the map.

answers.ask: Roughly how many puzzles per biome, and how many of them gate the castle?
answers.answer: Use three simple puzzles per biome, for nine total; one key puzzle from each biome gates the castle, while the others provide tokens, items, or heart rewards.

answers.ask: Is the castle open from the start with the boss locked inside, or is the castle itself gated?
answers.answer: The castle itself is gated until the player completes the required key puzzle in each of the three biomes.
